key_insight: A Petri-net execution harness can block unsafe LLM tool actions, but allowing every safe action need not minimize costly replanning.
engineering_relevance: Representing capabilities, approvals, and budgets as execution prerequisites makes tool authorization independent of an injected request’s wording.
method: Model tool execution with Petri nets and treat tool outcomes as uncontrollable.
Enforce safety with a conventional maximally permissive supervisor.
Refine allowed actions using proposer-dependent value thresholds to reduce inference-call costs from retries.
evidence_signal: Formal analysis shows the conventional supervisor can be arbitrarily more intrusive than a stricter safe one; synthesis for an autonomous release agent finds that safe deployment requires a refusable step after rollout begins.
watch_item: Safety transfer to the running system depends on four assumptions, while least-intrusive refinement requires a proposer model.
paper_title: Certified Execution Harness for Agentic AI: Safe and Least-Intrusive Petri-Net Supervisory Control Between Reasoning and Action
